meta.name: Design Career Copilot — Portfolio Review Rubric
meta.description: Simulates how a design lead evaluates portfolios for AI-native design roles. Used as the structured reasoning framework for AI analysis.
meta.review_philosophy: A design lead does not score aesthetics in isolation. They read for evidence of judgment: how problems were chosen, how constraints were navigated, how users were understood, how solutions were validated, and how work scaled beyond a single screen. For AI roles, they additionally probe whether the designer understands probabilistic systems, trust calibration, and the unique failure modes of AI products.
evidence_hierarchy: primary — artifacts shown in portfolio (screens, flows, code, research outputs)
secondary — narrative claims supported by adjacent artifacts
inferred — reasonable conclusions from role context and project type
absent — expected evidence not present; treated as a gap, not assumed negative

levels.label: not_evident
levels.definition: No credible evidence. Dimension is missing or contradicted by portfolio.

levels.label: emerging
levels.definition: Surface-level mention or weak artifacts. Judgment not demonstrated.

levels.label: competent
levels.definition: Clear evidence at expected level for the target seniority. Meets bar.

levels.label: strong
levels.definition: Multiple strong artifacts. Shows intentional tradeoffs and reflection.

levels.label: exceptional
levels.definition: Rare depth. Teaches the reviewer something. Signals staff-level thinking.

ai_product_designer.title: AI Product Designer
ai_product_designer.definition: Owns end-to-end product design for AI-powered features and products. Balances user value, model capabilities, and business goals.
ai_product_designer.primary_lens: Can this person shape AI products that people trust, adopt, and return to — not just demo well?
dealbreakers: No evidence of designing for AI-specific constraints (uncertainty, latency, errors)
Portfolio shows only visual polish with no product or outcome narrative
Cannot articulate why AI was the right solution vs. deterministic alternatives

ai_ux_designer.title: AI UX Designer
ai_ux_designer.definition: Specializes in interaction patterns, flows, and experience architecture for AI-assisted and AI-native interfaces.
ai_ux_designer.primary_lens: Can this person design experiences where humans and AI collaborate fluently — including when the AI is wrong?
dealbreakers: No exploration of AI failure states, loading, or confidence communication
Interaction patterns copied from generic chat UI with no original thinking
No evidence of usability testing or iteration on AI-specific flows

design_engineer.title: Design Engineer
design_engineer.definition: Bridges design and engineering. Ships high-fidelity interfaces, design systems, and interactive prototypes — often with production-quality code.
design_engineer.primary_lens: Can this person translate design intent into real, performant, maintainable product surfaces — including dynamic AI UI?
dealbreakers: Portfolio is image-only with no code, prototypes, or build artifacts
No evidence of component architecture or design system contribution
Cannot demonstrate responsive, accessible, or production-grade implementation

dimensions.name: Problem Framing & Strategy
dimensions.description: How the designer identifies, scopes, and prioritizes problems. Whether they connect work to user needs and business context.
what_design_lead_asks: Did they solve a real problem or a visual exercise?
Can they articulate constraints, stakeholders, and success criteria?
Do they show strategic prioritization — what they chose NOT to do?

judgment_criteria.question: Is the problem statement specific, user-centered, and bounded?
weak_signals: No context on why project existed

judgment_criteria.question: Does the designer connect work to product/business strategy?
strong_signals: Ties to company OKRs or market opportunity

judgment_criteria.question: For AI projects — is AI justified as the right approach?

red_flags: Starts with final UI, never explains the problem
Generic placeholder problem (e.g., 'improve UX')
Claims AI transformation with no capability analysis
green_flags: Connects design decisions to measurable outcomes

dimensions.name: User Research & Discovery
dimensions.description: Evidence that the designer understands users through research, synthesis, and validation — not assumptions.
what_design_lead_asks: How did they learn about user needs?
Did research actually influence design decisions?
For AI products — did they study mental models around automation and trust?

judgment_criteria.question: Are appropriate methods used and described?
weak_signals: Persona wallpaper with no research backing

judgment_criteria.question: Is raw data synthesized into actionable insights?
strong_signals: Affinity maps, insight statements, opportunity areas
weak_signals: Insights that don't connect to solutions

judgment_criteria.question: Does research address how users perceive AI behavior?

red_flags: No research evidence in complex product work
Personas appear stock/template
Research findings never referenced in design decisions

dimensions.name: Interaction & UX Design
dimensions.description: Quality of flows, information architecture, interaction patterns, and end-to-end experience coherence.
what_design_lead_asks: Can I follow the full user journey?
Are interaction patterns appropriate and consistent?
For AI — are latency, streaming, errors, and partial results handled?

judgment_criteria.question: Are critical paths shown end-to-end, including edge cases?
Is information architecture logical and scalable?
Are AI-specific interaction patterns well-designed?
weak_signals: Black-box AI with no user control

judgment_criteria.question: Do microinteractions serve comprehension and feedback?

red_flags: Only polished final screens, no flows
No empty/error/loading states for AI features
Chat UI with no information architecture

dimensions.name: Visual Design & Craft
dimensions.description: Typography, color, layout, visual hierarchy, and overall polish. Craft as a tool for clarity, not decoration.
what_design_lead_asks: Is the work legible and intentional?
Does visual hierarchy support task completion?
For AI outputs — is dense information made scannable?

judgment_criteria.question: Can users parse priority at a glance?
strong_signals: Content density managed for AI output

judgment_criteria.question: Are visual patterns consistent across the work shown?
Are AI-generated content and metadata presented clearly?
strong_signals: Differentiation of AI vs. user content
weak_signals: No visual distinction for AI suggestions

red_flags: Dribbble-style shots with no product context
Illegible typography in AI response areas
Inconsistent visual language within same project
green_flags: AI output is structured and scannable

dimensions.name: Systems Thinking & Scalability
dimensions.description: Ability to design patterns that scale across products, teams, and states — not one-off screens.
what_design_lead_asks: Will this approach hold at 10x scope?
Did they contribute to or create reusable patterns?
For AI — is there a pattern library for varied model behaviors?

judgment_criteria.question: Is there evidence of component/system-level thinking?
Are solutions abstracted into reusable patterns?
strong_signals: Pattern library for AI states (loading, error, partial)
weak_signals: No naming or organization of patterns

judgment_criteria.question: Does the designer explain how the solution scales?

red_flags: No system artifacts for senior-level candidates
Every screen is a unique snowflake
No consideration of multi-state AI components
green_flags: Shows how system evolved over time

dimensions.name: Technical Fluency & Implementation
dimensions.description: Understanding of engineering constraints and ability to ship or prototype with technical fidelity.
what_design_lead_asks: Do they understand what's buildable?
Can they collaborate effectively with engineering?
For design engineers — can they actually ship?

judgment_criteria.question: Do designs reflect real technical constraints?
Are there build artifacts proving execution ability?
Does the designer understand AI system constraints?
weak_signals: No plan for hallucination/wrong answers at system level

judgment_criteria.question: For design engineers — is code maintainable and intentional?

red_flags: Design engineer portfolio with zero code
No async/latency consideration in AI UX
Prototype links broken or placeholder
green_flags: AI pipeline awareness in design decisions

dimensions.name: Collaboration & Communication
dimensions.description: Evidence of cross-functional work, stakeholder alignment, critique reception, and design advocacy.
what_design_lead_asks: Did they work with PM, eng, research, and leadership?
Can they communicate design rationale to non-designers?
For AI products — did they align with ML/data stakeholders?

judgment_criteria.question: Is collaboration with other disciplines visible?
Did they navigate constraints from multiple stakeholders?
Did they collaborate with ML engineers, data scientists, or AI safety?
weak_signals: No ML stakeholder mention in AI project

red_flags: No evidence of working with others on complex projects
Claims sole authorship of enterprise AI product
No iteration from feedback
green_flags: Documents alignment with ML on capability boundaries

dimensions.name: Impact & Outcomes
dimensions.description: Measurable or qualifiable results. Did the work move user behavior, business metrics, or team capability?
what_design_lead_asks: What changed because of this work?
Are metrics credible and contextualized?
For AI — did adoption, trust, or task success improve?

judgment_criteria.question: Are outcomes specific, contextualized, and believable?
Do outcomes cover user, business, and craft/team impact?
Are AI feature outcomes measured appropriately?
weak_signals: Only model accuracy cited (not UX outcome)
No measurement of AI failure recovery

red_flags: Zero outcomes across all projects
Metrics without methodology
Claims impact on work that appears concept-only
green_flags: Specific metrics tied to design decisions
AI outcomes measure user task success, not just model benchmarks

dimensions.name: AI Product Sense
dimensions.description: Role-specific judgment about designing products powered by probabilistic, evolving models. The differentiator for AI design roles.
what_design_lead_asks: Do they understand AI is not a button — it's a behavior?
Have they designed for uncertainty, cost, safety, and trust?
Would I trust them to own an AI feature in production?

judgment_criteria.question: Are non-deterministic outputs handled with appropriate UX?
Can users understand, verify, and control AI behavior?
Is the human-AI division of labor intentional?
strong_signals: Human approval gates for high-stakes actions
AI accelerates drudgery, human owns judgment
weak_signals: Human only cleans up AI mess with no upstream design

judgment_criteria.question: Is input design treated as a core product surface?
Is there a loop for improving AI experience over time?
weak_signals: No plan for model updates breaking UX

judgment_criteria.question: Are harmful outputs, bias, and misuse considered?

red_flags: ChatGPT wrapper with no original AI UX thinking
No error/hallucination handling in any AI project
Automates high-stakes decisions without human review
Portfolio predates AI but claims AI expertise with no AI work
green_flags: Original AI interaction patterns beyond chat
Shows learning from AI-specific user failures

dimensions.name: Process Documentation & Storytelling
dimensions.description: How clearly the designer communicates their thinking process, iterations, and learnings.
what_design_lead_asks: Can I follow how they got from problem to solution?
Do they show dead ends and learning, not just wins?
Is the narrative respectful of my time?

judgment_criteria.question: Does the case study follow a clear, scannable arc?
Are exploration and iteration shown?
Does the designer reflect on what they'd do differently?

red_flags: Every project identical template with swapped images
No iteration shown for 6-month project
10-minute read with no outcome

dimensions.name: Portfolio Presentation & Professionalism
dimensions.description: Overall portfolio as a product: curation, accessibility, contact clarity, and attention to detail.
what_design_lead_asks: Did they curate their best, most relevant work?
Is this portfolio easy to review in 15–20 minutes?
Are there typos, broken links, or NDA violations?

judgment_criteria.question: Is work selected and ordered for the target role?
weak_signals: Student work mixed with senior claims
No AI work for AI role application

judgment_criteria.question: Can a busy design lead review efficiently?
strong_signals: Reasonable file size and load time

judgment_criteria.question: Are basics handled correctly?

red_flags: Broken portfolio
No relevant work for applied role
Confidential client data unredacted

evaluation_synthesis.description: How a design lead forms a final hire/no-hire recommendation from dimensional scores.

steps.name: role_calibration
steps.action: Load role_profile for target role. Apply dimension_weights and identify critical_dimensions and dealbreakers.

steps.name: evidence_extraction
steps.action: For each dimension, extract evidence_to_extract from portfolio PDF and JD. Tag each artifact: primary | secondary | inferred | absent.

steps.name: dimensional_scoring
steps.action: Score each dimension 1–5 using judgment_criteria. For each score, cite specific evidence. Apply seniority_calibration from JD.

steps.name: dealbreaker_check
steps.action: If any role dealbreaker or dimension red_flag cluster is triggered, cap overall recommendation regardless of average score.

steps.name: weighted_match_score
steps.action: Compute match_score = sum(dimension_score / 5 * dimension_weight) * 100, rounded to integer.

steps.name: critical_dimension_gate
steps.action: If any critical_dimension scores below meets_bar for target seniority, downgrade recommendation one tier even if match_score is high.

steps.name: jd_skill_mapping
steps.action: Parse JD into required_skills and nice_to_have_skills. Map each skill to one or more dimensions. Produce skill_coverage matrix: strong | partial | missing.

steps.name: gap_analysis
steps.action: Identify top gaps where JD requires skill but evidence is absent or weak. Rank by impact: high (critical dimension + required skill), medium, low.

steps.name: strengths_weaknesses_synthesis
steps.action: Strengths = dimensions scoring strong/exceptional with primary evidence. Weaknesses = dimensions scoring emerging/not_evident OR absent required evidence.

steps.name: executive_summary
steps.action: Write 3–5 sentence summary: overall fit, standout strength, primary concern, hire recommendation tier (strong_yes | yes | mixed | no), and confidence level based on evidence density.

steps.name: action_plan
steps.action: Generate prioritized, actionable recommendations tied to specific gaps. Each action must reference a dimension and include estimated effort.

recommendation_tiers.criteria: match_score >= 80, all critical_dimensions meet bar, no dealbreakers, 2+ dimensions exceptional
match_score >= 65, all critical_dimensions meet bar, no dealbreakers
match_score 45–64 OR one critical_dimension below bar OR significant gaps in required JD skills
match_score < 45 OR dealbreaker triggered OR 2+ critical_dimensions below bar

confidence_modifiers.high: 3+ case studies with primary evidence across critical dimensions
confidence_modifiers.medium: 1–2 solid case studies; some dimensions inferred
confidence_modifiers.low: Thin portfolio, mostly absent evidence, heavy inference required

output_schema.description: Structured shape the AI reviewer must return after applying this rubric.

fields.reviewer_notes: string — internal reasoning the lead would share in a hiring debrief
